title: versions/<versionId>/version.json — what this version is
description:
Written once by the analyzer, when a version is established, and never touched again. A version is one cut or presentation of a movie or episode — theatrical and director's cut, colour and black-and-white, HDR and SDR — and its folder is the one place its media lives: the original file, the package made from it, or both.

Every version is a folder. There is no version in the item folder itself, and a re-package is a new version folder, never an edit of this one.

The marks live here rather than in any file, so they survive the original's deletion and apply to every package of the version. What plays by default is not here: that is behaviour, and the database owns it.

Paths: originalFile is a plain name in THIS folder. sourceIds name records at the item level (sources/<sourceId>.json).

versionId.description: Equals the name of the folder this file sits in.

createdBy.description: The service or person that established the version.

edition.description: Which cut this is, and what says so.

label.description: Edition wording as published, e.g. 'Roadshow Director's Cut'.

colour.description: Measured from the picture, not from a label.

runtimeMs.description: Measured from the original. Deliberately not the runtime a reference database publishes — that is one runtime for every cut, and it belongs to the metadata projection.

chapters.description: Chapter marks on this version's timeline.

chaptersFrom.description: Where the chapter marks came from; null when there are none.

segments.description: Intro, recap and credits ranges on this version's timeline, each with the detector that found it.

sourceIds.description: The originals this version was made from — several when it is split into parts. Each names sources/<sourceId>.json at the item level, which stays after the file itself is gone.

originalFile.description: The original placed in THIS folder next to its package, under its own name — or null when the version was made without keeping it here. Written once: when the original is deleted later, this keeps naming it and an events/…-original-deleted.json record says it is gone.

decision.description: A conclusion with its confidence and who reached it. There is no review field: a record written once cannot carry a task, and what a person still has to look at belongs in the database.
